answer: A relic atlas guards an agent economy with a maze drawn in umber ink: every new identity must walk a maze whose corridors double each time, so the first fake walks 2 corridors, the second 4, the third 8, the tenth 1,024 and the twentieth 1,048,576, and twenty fakes together walk 2,097,150. Bulk farming fails because one cartographer draws each maze by hand and the exit of one maze is the entrance of the next, so no maze can be walked early, in parallel, or bought solved; the pulse of the network beats one maze at a time, like a single guide leading one traveller through one labyrinth.
